data.why: The repo ships ready-to-open Pajek (.net) and JSON network files matching the GUI's 'Open' format handlers; edge-cases.net is a small hand-written Pajek file adding an isolated vertex, a self-loop, and a disconnected pair to probe how the density/clustering/shortest-path/diameter calculations handle degenerate graphs.

goals: Load a network file (Pajek .net or JSON) and visualize its graph layout using force-directed or no-overlap algorithms
Compute basic graph properties: vertex/edge counts, density, average degree, average clustering coefficient
Compute average shortest path length, diameter, and global efficiency for the loaded network
Inspect per-vertex detail: degree, clustering coefficient, and centrality for every node
Compare topologies (complete, random, scale-free, small-world, hybrid) by generating or loading each and contrasting their summary statistics
Export results as a Pajek file, JSON file, SVG graph image, or an HTML properties report

review.summary: The tree describes CNATool's purpose well: load a network, lay it out, compute global and per-vertex properties, compare with reference topologies, and export. Most of the cited screens back up their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: synthetic-network generation and the GPU/manual-layout claims are missing or only in side notes, the Directed Graph task overstates what was seen, and the export and replay evidence can't be fully checked from this folder.
